svg.font-family: Familjen Grotesk, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif
svg.text: Right to left, consonants only, joined on a baseline, tense in the hand. New: dz and sh, so Kord names can be spelled.
20 letters. Farsi-led: flowing joined strokes, shared shapes told apart by dots, tails and teeth, with a little Cyrillic left in the straight stems.
The tooth carries b, p, t, n, y by dot count and position. The hanging bowl carries h, kh. The tail carries r, z. The hooked stroke carries d, g.
Three teeth carry s, sh and ts: a dot above the teeth makes the hacek. The dz ligature is a d stem rising from the baseline, with the z tail and its dot beside it.
The word is MLK, king. Present is the plain stroke; the rest modify it. The two grades inside past and future are my proposal.
Everyday writing, added after the Closing. Vowels sit above for the deep class and below for the forward class. Tense gets its own sign at the start of the word.
Samples. The root is MLK, king, with vowels and a tense sign.
"The stone is hard" in the Kord hand
Stone is KL, hard is KS. A verb is always infinitive, so it always takes the curled caps. Only the noun changes hand.
This stone is hard, right now.
Stone, as a kind, is hard. Always.
Read right to left. The rightmost word is the noun, which changes hand. The verb to its left never does.
The two Kord names the old draft could not write
Canon: Sahdzakoda (Gold) and Šohdzakoda (Onyx, s with a hacek). Vowels are carried as refugee marks.
Onyx Kord: the s carries a hacek, drawn as a dotted s
Hall is koda and the blood marker dza is the Latvian-shaped affricate, so dz is the letter every Kord seat leans on. A dotted s keeps sh apart from s.
